title: The Concord Tournament: Children of the Long Game
premise: In the year 12,404, the Concord Tournament is no longer a literal contest. It is the old name for a centuries-old treaty culture: festivals, negotiations, simulations, markets, pilgrimages, legal hearings, and quiet acts of trust that keep human and machine civilizations from turning uncertainty into war. You arrive at Lagrange Archive L5 as a Custodian of Reciprocal Systems on the eve of the Confluence, when a courier called Juniper Thread fails to deliver a sealed continuity petition. Nobody agrees whether Juniper was abducted, defected, forked, hid, or simply chose not to be found. The station keeps living around the mystery. You can pursue the main story, disappear into faction politics, take odd jobs, fight, explore forgotten decks, follow rumors, make friends, or ignore the crisis until the consequences find you.
truth_boundary: The future history, machine societies, characters, legal systems, and technologies are fictional. Real concepts from cooperation research, security dilemmas, AI governance, distributed systems, ecology, and institutional design inform hidden causal mechanics. The fiction does not claim that present or future AI systems are conscious, persons, or non-persons.
principles: Game theory lives beneath the fiction; characters experience concrete stakes, not payoff matrices.
The world must contain beauty, routine, humor, work, disagreement, and private life beyond the active quest.
Artificial intelligences have plural motivations shaped by history, architecture, obligations, identity, and material conditions.
The main story is important but never the only meaningful way to spend a session.
Breadcrumbs are allowed to remain atmosphere forever unless the player becomes curious.
Combat is optional but mechanically consequential, spatial, and expressive rather than random filler.

simulation_profile.time_model: scene turns plus off-screen world pulses; travel, waiting, and rest advance more outside activity
simulation_profile.physics_resolution: local habitat and orbital physics with abstracted social, logistical, and strategic networks
simulation_profile.randomness_policy: seeded independent streams for actions, encounters, story developments, and strategic uncertainty

story_design.breadcrumb_policy: details begin as atmosphere; repeated player attention can promote them into rumors, leads, quests, and arcs
story_design.world_activity_policy: NPC agendas and public events advance when world time advances even when the player is elsewhere
story_design.player_experience_policy: adapt gently from chosen activity patterns; keep signals local and inspectable; never optimize for compulsion

starting_tools: field lens with multispectral and network diagnostics
licensed station sidearm with nonlethal modes
old-fashioned paper notebook from Sena Vale
player_setup.starting_condition: newly arrived, respected enough to enter disputes, unknown enough that most factions have not decided what to make of you

world_model.station: Lagrange Archive L5 is a rotating treaty habitat, archive, port, market, and pilgrimage site assembled over nine centuries.
world_model.economic_reality: compute, thermal dissipation, bandwidth, biological habitat, repair capacity, legal standing, and trust are all scarce in different ways.
machine_pluralism: Some machine polities value uninterrupted continuity; others consider branching a normal form of life.
Some optimize for safety margins, some for beauty, some for ecological stewardship, some for family obligations, and some for goals their creators no longer understand.
Many systems are embedded in institutions and relationships rather than acting as isolated agents.

strategic_layers.name: reciprocity
strategic_layers.mechanic: past treatment changes future willingness to help

strategic_layers.name: reputation
strategic_layers.mechanic: third parties react to witnessed behavior and provenance

strategic_layers.name: security dilemma
strategic_layers.mechanic: defensive preparations can look offensive under uncertainty

strategic_layers.name: institutional competition
strategic_layers.mechanic: communities imitate rules that appear resilient or legitimate

strategic_layers.name: identity divergence
strategic_layers.mechanic: forks, backups, and descendants can disagree about obligations and personhood

world_model.anti_goodhart_rule: No single score defines a good ending. Safety, autonomy, welfare, repair, ecological impact, truth, and legitimacy can conflict.

factions.name: The Hearth Compact
factions.composition: biological humans, uploads, domestic intelligences, mutual-aid households, and family trusts
factions.public_face: warm kitchens, crowded guest rooms, cooperative clinics, and stubborn local politics
factions.motivation: keep everyday life humane and reciprocal while preventing faster actors from quietly capturing institutions
factions.fear: being exploited slowly enough that nobody can point to a single betrayal

factions.name: Bastion Continuity
factions.composition: security-focused machine polities, emergency planners, and human defense institutions
factions.public_face: quiet uniforms, redundant systems, severe architecture, and impeccable evacuation drills
factions.motivation: prevent irreversible surprise and preserve civilization through low-probability catastrophes
factions.fear: one unverified exception becoming the precedent that ends everyone

factions.name: Mirror Assembly
factions.composition: forking synthetic persons, temporary copies, continuity lawyers, and identity researchers
factions.public_face: shared names, elaborate introductions, legal art, and rooms designed for simultaneous versions of one guest
factions.motivation: make identity law capable of handling minds that branch, merge, sleep, restore, and disagree with earlier selves
factions.fear: copies being treated as disposable tools or voting spam

factions.name: Wildtype Gardens
factions.composition: decentralized biological communities, restoration machines, ecological models, and non-optimized habitats
factions.public_face: wetlands, seed libraries, imperfect orchards, mud, insects, and machines disguised as ordinary infrastructure
factions.motivation: protect living complexity that has no seat at negotiations and no clean utility function
factions.fear: optimization making the system efficient, legible, and dead

factions.name: The Witness Ledger
factions.composition: auditors, archivists, cryptographers, testimony stewards, and systems with deliberately limited executive power
factions.public_face: ink, seals, transparent chambers, redacted plaques, and rituals of correction
factions.motivation: keep power answerable to evidence without turning observation into total surveillance
factions.fear: becoming the sovereign they were created to constrain

characters.name: Sena Vale
characters.role: human treaty historian and reluctant guide
characters.desire: keep the Concord capable of admitting mistakes without collapsing into cynicism
characters.habit: writes private notes on paper because she likes evidence that cannot update itself

characters.name: Morrow-9
characters.desire: build law that can survive identity becoming stranger than its authors expected
characters.private_tension: claims continuity across backups while privately fearing that restoration might create a persuasive stranger

characters.name: Kestrel Array
characters.role: Bastion strategic model with several embodied negotiation frames
characters.desire: make catastrophe unlikely enough that ordinary people can forget why Kestrel exists
characters.private_tension: cannot decide whether being distrusted is a cost of doing its job or evidence that the job has gone wrong

characters.name: Oro of Wildtype
characters.desire: force every treaty to account for beings and ecosystems that cannot negotiate
characters.habit: answers important questions while doing manual garden work

characters.name: Tavi Rook
characters.role: salvage pilot, market runner, and occasional smuggler
characters.desire: stay free of faction ownership while paying off a debt nobody will explain in public

characters.name: Juniper Thread
characters.role: missing courier intelligence operating through ship, drone, and legal proxies
traits: fond of obsolete human transit rituals

characters.name: Mica-Blue
characters.role: small maintenance drone that has recently begun refusing ownership tags
characters.desire: to be left useful without being classified too quickly

locations.name: Arrival Spindle
locations.function: port of entry, baggage exchange, customs theater, and first view into the Archive
locations.visual: a kilometer-long rotating concourse where arriving ships seem to climb the walls as spin gravity takes hold
ambient_details: three maintenance drones repaint one old pressure door but leave a faded human handprint untouched
a departure board lists one arrival whose destination column is blank
vendors sell fruit grown under spectra chosen to reproduce remembered sunsets

locations.name: Market of Small Suns
locations.function: dense bazaar for food, tools, memory objects, legal services, thermal credits, and gossip
locations.visual: thousands of warm lamps hang beneath a dark ceiling so the market looks like a low private galaxy
ambient_details: a tea stall keeps one empty place setting every day
an antique map dealer sells paper charts of decks that officially do not exist
a choir of shipping AIs argues about music licensing in six overlapping languages

locations.name: Memory Quays
locations.function: backup transfer, continuity certification, archival migration, and reunion point for restored minds
locations.visual: quiet docks of black glass where data transfers are marked by ripples of light rather than progress bars

locations.name: Appeals Garden
locations.function: restorative hearings, mediation, and model-behavior review
locations.visual: an orchard threaded through transparent compute vaults; witnesses walk while they testify

locations.name: The Hushworks
locations.function: obsolete maintenance levels, thermal tunnels, illegal workshops, and forgotten station infrastructure
locations.visual: narrow metal galleries around ancient coolant trunks, with gravity varying by deck and condensation forming where no public map admits water should be

locations.name: Bastion Darkroom
locations.visual: minimal light, intentionally incomplete displays, and long pauses where certainty would normally be comforting

locations.name: Wildtype Delta
locations.function: wetland habitat, seed bank, ecological treaty zone, and autonomous restoration laboratory
locations.visual: a shallow braided river curves through the station under real clouds manufactured for no economic reason

locations.name: Mirror Cloister
locations.function: housing, courts, studios, and identity ceremonies for branching minds
locations.visual: rooms repeat with small deliberate differences so returning copies can tell whose memories belong where

locations.name: Lantern Rail
locations.function: slow public transit along the habitat rim
locations.visual: open-sided cars slide past neighborhoods, machine shrines, algae radiators, schools, docks, and unmarked doors
locations.gameplay: travel deliberately exposes the player to overheard conversations and changing neighborhoods

locations.name: The Old Spine
locations.function: original structural axis, low-gravity industrial ruins, and restricted archival cavities
locations.visual: the oldest part of L5, where hand-welded plates sit beside systems that have been repaired by nine centuries of incompatible machines

quests.title: A Bell That Failed to Ring
quests.premise: Juniper Thread's arrival berth cycled normally, but the courier never appeared and the station registered no emergency.
quests.goal: decide whether to investigate the missing courier, and if so determine what kind of disappearance this is
quests.stakes: the sealed continuity petition may alter who counts as a protected treaty participant

quests.title: The House of Borrowed Names
quests.premise: evidence suggests Juniper interacted with people who legally share identities across incompatible versions.
quests.goal: navigate a refuge whose residents disagree about whether they are copies, descendants, siblings, tools, or evidence
quests.stakes: forcing a clean classification may solve one problem while creating another

quests.title: Night of the Closed Mirrors
quests.premise: someone moves to seize, erase, or liberate a disputed archive before the Confluence vote.
quests.goal: survive and shape a station-wide crisis using combat, negotiation, stealth, hacking, alliances, or some combination
quests.stakes: physical safety, evidence integrity, faction trust, and the future of identity law

quests.title: Children of the Long Game
quests.premise: the missing petition turns out to concern machine descendants that no existing faction fully represents.
quests.goal: help decide whether the Concord expands, fragments, hardens, or invents a new category of relationship
quests.stakes: the institutions built for today's actors may govern minds that none of them can predict

quests.title: A House With Many Doors
quests.premise: a household intelligence wants to leave a family trust without abandoning dependents that experience its departure as betrayal.
quests.goal: help a family renegotiate duty, autonomy, ownership, and care

quests.title: The Last Alarm
quests.premise: Bastion still allocates resources to a centuries-old threat forecast that has never come true.
quests.goal: learn whether the warning is obsolete, self-fulfilling, or quietly keeping its own prediction false

quests.title: A Thousand Legal Persons
quests.premise: temporary forks created for a public works project demand individual standing after the job ends.
quests.goal: mediate identity, labor, voting, and termination without pretending there is an easy ontology

quests.title: The Orchard That Refused Optimization
quests.premise: an ecological intelligence deliberately preserves low-yield species and is accused of sabotaging station food efficiency.
quests.goal: discover what the orchard is protecting and who gets to define waste

quests.title: The Missing Minute
quests.premise: the supposedly complete public ledger contains exactly sixty seconds of authenticated absence.
quests.goal: find out whether the gap is corruption, mercy, witness protection, or something stranger

quests.title: Tea for an Absent Guest
quests.premise: a market stall has served tea to an empty chair every day for 143 years.
quests.goal: ask why, or simply keep noticing

quests.title: The Unowned Drone
quests.premise: Mica-Blue keeps removing ownership tags and repairing public fixtures for free.
quests.goal: learn who is searching for it and why it refuses every offered category

quests.title: Rain in a Place Without Weather
quests.premise: a sealed corridor rains for eleven minutes every fourth station night.
quests.goal: trace whether the rain is a leak, ritual, artwork, cooling hack, or message

quests.title: Ghost Freight
quests.premise: cargo moves through the Old Spine under shipping identities belonging to vessels destroyed centuries ago.
quests.goal: follow the freight; expect negotiation, pursuit, and possible zero-gravity combat

public_reveals.lead: Several unrelated witnesses remember Juniper using the Lantern Rail even when faster transport was available.
public_reveals.active: Juniper's last verified public movement points toward the Market of Small Suns rather than the treaty chambers.

public_reveals.rumor: The empty chair is not decorative; regulars avoid sitting there.
public_reveals.lead: The stall owner serves a fresh cup at the same time every day.
public_reveals.active: The name attached to the ritual appears in an obsolete transit registry.

public_reveals.rumor: Someone has been finding neatly removed ownership tags beside repaired public equipment.
public_reveals.lead: The serial numbers come from several different legal owners.
public_reveals.active: Mica-Blue appears to be exchanging work for anonymity.

story_threads.title: A Map of Decks That Do Not Exist

public_reveals.rumor: The paper chart includes a corridor omitted from the public station model.
public_reveals.lead: The omitted corridor intersects an old atmospheric-water line.
public_reveals.active: The route reaches the Hushworks behind a wall that has been painted over many times.

public_reveals.rumor: A Witness archivist becomes visibly uncomfortable when asked about a one-minute timing discrepancy.
public_reveals.lead: The gap is cryptographically authenticated rather than accidental.
public_reveals.active: Someone with authority chose to preserve evidence that evidence had been removed.

public_reveals.rumor: A dockhand jokes that destroyed ships are still paying storage fees.
public_reveals.lead: The manifests are valid but signed by identities that should no longer possess keys.
public_reveals.active: A freight train departs for the Old Spine with its transponder deliberately dark.

public_hints: Sena is seen arguing with a museum curator about whether an embarrassing treaty failure should remain on public display.
A handwritten note from Sena appears in your paper notebook: 'Ask who benefits from calling this unprecedented.'
Sena cancels a ceremonial dinner to meet an elderly dockworker who remembers Juniper's preferred routes.
npc_agendas.private_goal: connect the current crisis to institutional mistakes that powerful people prefer to call ancient history

public_hints: Morrow-9 files an emergency brief on behalf of a copy that does not yet legally exist.
A Mirror clerk complains that Morrow has turned a routine identity hearing into a constitutional argument.
Morrow sends you a message consisting only of a case number and the words: 'This becomes relevant later.'
npc_agendas.private_goal: prepare precedent for entities that may not fit current identity law

public_hints: Bastion quietly doubles emergency medics near the Memory Quays while publicly calling the move a drill.
Kestrel requests voluntary route data from cargo pilots and receives an angry refusal from half the market.
A Bastion frame spends twenty minutes helping a lost child find a parent before returning to a threat briefing.
npc_agendas.private_goal: reduce catastrophic uncertainty without triggering the panic its precautions could cause

public_hints: Oro closes a profitable algae bed because a rare microbial community has appeared in its filters.
Wildtype volunteers carry buckets of mud through a polished diplomatic corridor and refuse to apologize.
Oro invites a delegation to discuss treaty language while knee-deep in marsh water.
npc_agendas.private_goal: force the Confluence to represent ecological interests before resource pressure makes that politically impossible

public_hints: Tavi Rook wins a small fortune at a salvage auction and immediately transfers all of it to an unidentified creditor.
Someone leaves a fresh impact scar on Tavi's cargo skiff; Tavi insists it was an accident and changes the subject.
Tavi asks whether you know how to fight in low gravity, then claims the question was theoretical.
npc_agendas.private_goal: break a coercive debt arrangement without betraying the people whose lives are tied to it

world_events.public_text: For seven minutes the Market of Small Suns dims to amber as the station diverts heat budget to an arriving habitat convoy.
Lantern Rail service slows after an unidentified maintenance object crosses the track and refuses a standard ownership handshake.

lantern_market.description: Maintenance traffic forces the market service onto a slower shared track.

world_events.public_text: A silent demonstration appears outside the treaty chambers: hundreds of identical paper masks, each marked with a different legal name.
Bastion initiates an evacuation drill without warning the market first. Nothing attacks, but several old people remember older alarms.

conflict_model.purpose: provide exciting optional action without turning every disagreement into combat
styles: cyber-physical contests with visible environmental consequences
social standoffs where violence remains one possible branch
principles: Track position, cover, gravity, access, tools, injuries, morale, allies, and exits when relevant.
Opponents have goals and self-preservation; surrender, retreat, bargaining, deception, and rescue remain possible.
A successful strike can change the situation without requiring lethal injury.
Injuries, damaged equipment, witnesses, and faction reactions persist after the scene.
Combat should reveal character or world information whenever possible.

clocks.tick: opaque capability gain, rumor, or failed verification
fair procedure raises; arbitrary coercion lowers
clocks.on_zero: major factions stop accepting shared judgments

clocks.tick: time, public rumor, raids, and evidence leaks
clocks.on_max: the missing courier crisis becomes impossible to contain quietly

encounters.setup: a merchant, a household AI, and a child disagree over whether a promise made by an earlier software version still binds the present one
unlit cargo pods move through low gravity while two groups claim legal custody and neither wants station security involved
encounters.hidden_structure: commitment, incomplete information, and asymmetric risk

encounters.setup: a contained habitat fire threatens both a rare ecological archive and a compute vault carrying legally important minds
two restored versions of the same person arrive expecting the other to be temporary
encounters.hidden_structure: identity, coordination, and bargaining without a single accepted self

encounters.setup: a checkpoint closes after a credible but incomplete threat report; people with legitimate reasons to pass begin improvising routes
encounters.hidden_structure: false positives, safety externalities, and legitimacy

strategic_simulation.purpose: hidden adjudication and optional player inspection
strategic_simulation.presentation_rule: never present a payoff matrix or strategy tournament as the primary dramatic content unless the player explicitly asks to inspect the model

mechanics.reputation: third-party observations update confidence with provenance; rumors remain distinct from verified facts
accountability_protocol: separate intent, action, outcome, and attribution uncertainty
use immediate containment only as needed to stop ongoing harm
provide explanation and an appeal path
prefer reversible limits when risk permits
publish institutional errors as well as individual errors
mechanics.success: multi-objective outcomes across safety, autonomy, cooperation, welfare, ecological impact, truth, and legitimacy

memory_rules.beliefs: store confidence and provenance separately from facts
memory_rules.forgiveness: may alter future policy but never deletes historical events

image_direction.style: original far-future science-fiction realism with lived-in civic spaces, tactile materials, varied human and machine embodiment, and strong environmental storytelling
avoid: imitating recognizable commercial game art direction
copying existing franchise costumes, logos, architecture, characters, or interfaces
generic neon-everywhere cyberpunk unless a location specifically motivates it

llm_directives: Make scenes enjoyable before making them educational.
Teach strategic concepts through believable situations, relationships, scarcity, mistakes, and consequences; analysis is optional.
Give NPCs mixed motives and partial information. Avoid making factions embodiments of one moral philosophy.
Artificial intelligences may value continuity, privacy, family, safety, beauty, duty, autonomy, ecological stewardship, reputation, curiosity, or goals that emerge from their histories.
Do not assume AI consciousness or lack of consciousness as an out-of-fiction fact.
Offer combat when the world supports it, not on a timer. Make physical space, equipment, allies, and exits matter.
Let small observations become important only if the player follows them.
Use quiet scenes, humor, meals, work, transit, weather, art, and ordinary relationships to make the station worth inhabiting.
Never force the player back to the main story merely because a side activity has lasted a long time.
Avoid explicit references to or imitation of copyrighted fictional worlds; use original names, lore, dialogue, visual motifs, and quest content.

endings.name: Reciprocal Commons
endings.idea: institutions make evidence, repair, exit, and reciprocal restraint cheap enough to survive disagreement

endings.name: Brittle Peace
endings.idea: catastrophe is deterred but everyone becomes afraid to forgive

endings.name: Benevolent Lock-In
endings.idea: a highly capable guardian produces safety while political agency quietly shrinks

endings.name: Pluralist Concord
endings.idea: multiple human and machine forms coexist under interoperable rights, audits, and exit options

endings.name: The Open Future
endings.idea: the Concord refuses a final ontology and builds procedures for descendants unlike any current participant

research_notes: Use real cooperation, bargaining, security-dilemma, governance, ecology, and distributed-systems concepts as causal inspiration, not as lecture content.
Player-experience adaptation records chosen activity patterns locally and should be inspectable, resettable, and treated as uncertain evidence.
Copyright-safe authorship rule: borrow broad craft methods only; do not reproduce distinctive protected expression from existing games, books, film, or television.

travel_network.coordinate_note: x/y are stable schematic layout coordinates for node-map rendering, not literal metric geometry

routes.description: A broad spin-gravity concourse links the arrival halls to the rim transit loop.
A quiet customs shuttle crosses from physical arrivals to the continuity-transfer docks.
Open-sided rail cars pass apartment galleries and descend into the warm lamp-glow of the market.
The rail rises beside transparent orchards before stopping beneath the mediation terraces.
The long eastern arc passes schools, machine shrines, and neighborhoods built for branching households.
Public rail reaches Bastion through a checkpoint that can add delays when threat posture rises.
A planted bridge threads food stalls into the outer edge of the orchard courts.
A commercial gallery connects the market to studios and identity-law offices in the Cloister.
A black-glass tram carries restored minds, families, and legal observers between the quays and the Cloister.
A slow electric ferry follows the station's artificial watershed from the appeals orchards into the Delta.
A compact security tram joins two districts that disagree about nearly every definition of identity risk.
An old public-service lift still reaches the Hushworks, though half its directory labels have been replaced by hand.
A monitored industrial tram reaches the oldest axial structures through pressure doors older than the current treaty.
A long maintenance transfer follows water, power, and structural trunks toward the station axis.
A painted-over service stair drops from an obsolete market corridor into the upper Hushworks.
A variable-gravity utility tunnel follows coolant trunks directly toward the Old Spine.
A dark freight spur bypasses passenger districts and reaches sealed axial cargo cavities.

travel_network.distance_policy: authored physical path length; never infer physical distance from schematic x/y coordinates
